title: About the CSOE exam
description: What the Certified Sarbanes-Oxley Expert (CSOE) exam looks like, how its questions work, how to use an open book against a short clock, how to buy the program and sit the exam online, and how passing turns into a certificate. Written in plain language by KaiSip from SOXCPA's published pages, with the law cited at its public source.
disclaimer: KaiSip is an independent study app. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by or sponsored by the Sarbanes Oxley Compliance Professionals Association (SOXCPA), the SEC, the PCAOB or COSO. SOXCPA alone sets the CSOE exam rules and decides who is certified. KaiSip's questions are original and are not SOXCPA's. No study app can promise a pass, including this one.
check_before_booking: Prices, attempt rules and exam terms on this page were checked on the date shown. They can change, so check sarbanes-oxley-association.com before you book or buy.

sections.title: The exam at a glance
sections.summary: An online, open-book exam of 35 multiple-choice questions in 90 minutes. You need 70% or higher to pass, and the exam moves forward only.
items: 35 questions in 90 minutes, about 2.5 minutes each. You sit it online from home or office, in any country.
Each question is either a direct question or an incomplete statement to complete, followed by four possible responses. You choose the best one.
The pass mark is 70% or higher, which means at least 25 correct answers out of 35.
The exam is open book: you may use your study materials while you answer.
It moves forward only. You cannot go back to change an answer, skip a question or stop and resume later.
Running past 90 minutes, or closing the browser before you finish, counts as an unsuccessful attempt.
SOXCPA says the exam asks only what its official presentations clearly answer. The presentations are 1,022 slides, delivered as downloadable PDFs.
SOXCPA sends no sample questions or past exams, and your exam is not available for review afterward.

sources.label: SOXCPA: Questions about the certification and the exams (PDF)

sections.title: The five domains and their weights
sections.summary: SOXCPA publishes no domain weights. KaiSip groups SOXCPA's five course parts into five domains and weights each by its share of the course's topic lines, so the weights are KaiSip's estimate.

domains.name: Scope and reach of the Act
Internal control frameworks and SOX scope

items: Domain 1 covers which companies and people the Act reaches: issuers, filer categories, foreign private issuers, registration, EDGAR and American Depositary Receipts (ADRs).
Domain 2 covers the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (PCAOB) and the Act's auditor independence rules, such as prohibited services, preapproval and partner rotation.
Domain 3 covers audit committees, the officer certifications in Sections 302 and 906, management's internal control report under Section 404 and the other disclosure duties.
Domain 4 covers the SEC, its investigations and settlements, the records and fraud crimes, whistleblower protection and the Dodd-Frank Act's changes.
Domain 5 covers the COSO internal control and enterprise risk frameworks, and what falls within SOX scope, such as spreadsheets and service organizations.
Domains 4 and 5 are the largest in KaiSip's estimate, at 27% each. SOXCPA does not say how much of the exam comes from each part.
KaiSip's notes do not yet cover the course's EU and Japanese counterparts to SOX (E-SOX and J-SOX), because their official sources could not be opened. Study those parts in SOXCPA's presentations.

sections.title: How CSOE questions are built
sections.summary: SOXCPA describes two question forms, each with four responses, and asks for the best answer. The text of the law and the rules decides; there is no role to play.
items: Each question has two parts: a question or an incomplete statement, then four possible responses. An incomplete statement ends mid-sentence, and the right response completes it.
SOXCPA's instructions say to look for the best answer, not merely a correct one, and to cross out the responses you know are wrong before choosing among the rest.
The exam asks only what the official presentations clearly answer. Those cover the Act title by title, the SEC and the PCAOB, the COSO frameworks and the Dodd-Frank amendments.
KaiSip's pattern: the key is what a section or rule requires, of whom, by when and with what consequence. Good practice that the rule does not demand is usually a distractor.
KaiSip's pattern: wrong options are often real rules that answer a nearby question, such as Section 302 against 906, 404(a) against 404(b), or the SEC against the PCAOB.
SOXCPA's instructions do not describe priority words. When a question uses BEST, FIRST or MOST, it is ranking options; when it names a section, ask what that section requires.
SOXCPA's steps PDF for its EU program describes the same format in the same words, so this is a shared exam template.
KaiSip's practice questions are original and follow the published format only. They are not SOXCPA's questions and do not come from its exam.

sections.title: Using an open book well
sections.summary: The exam is open book, but 90 minutes for 35 questions leaves little time to search. Recall is your main tool, and a lookup is your backup for one exact fact.
items: SOXCPA explains its open-book choice: at work, compliance staff consult regulations and frameworks, so the exam tests understanding and application rather than memory.
Open book does not mean slow. With about 2.5 minutes a question and no going back, searching for every answer runs out the clock.
KaiSip's pattern: know who acts and which rule applies without looking. Save lookups for an exact number, date or threshold you cannot pin down.
Before exam day, make your own one-page list of the numbers that matter: deadlines, thresholds, penalty tiers and retention periods, each with its section.
SOXCPA's FAQ suggests marking up its PDFs with highlights, sticky notes, bookmarks and keyword search. Set these up while you study, not during the exam.
SOXCPA advises studying the presentations at least twice and estimates about 29 hours of study on average.
Practice answering from memory first. It shows you which facts you know and which still need a lookup.

sections.title: Pacing a forward-only exam
sections.summary: 90 minutes for 35 questions is about 2.5 minutes each. The exam moves forward only, so every answer is final when you give it.
items: No going back: you cannot return to review or change an earlier answer. The browser's back button only reloads the current page.
No skipping: you answer every question in the order it appears.
No pause: you cannot stop and resume. Closing the browser loses your answers and counts as an unsuccessful attempt.
Finish within 90 minutes. A result past the time limit is marked as an unsuccessful attempt.
KaiSip's pattern: aim for about 2 minutes a question, reaching question 15 at 30 minutes and question 30 at the hour, which keeps time for a few lookups.
If a question stalls you, cross out what you know is wrong, choose the best of the rest and move on. You cannot come back to it.

sections.title: Common traps by domain
sections.summary: Each domain has a few traps that catch prepared candidates. Most give a duty to the wrong actor, apply an old version of a rule or choose good practice over the rule. These are KaiSip's patterns.
items: Scope and reach: applying every duty to every issuer. Check filer status first; non-accelerated filers and emerging growth companies skip the auditor's attestation under Section 404(b), but not management's report.
Scope and reach: assuming private companies are wholly outside the Act. Crimes written for anyone, such as destroying records to obstruct a federal investigation, reach their staff too.
PCAOB and independence: treating the PCAOB as a regulator of public companies, or a Board rule as binding once adopted. It oversees audit firms, and its rules need SEC approval.
PCAOB and independence: thinking audit committee preapproval can permit a prohibited non-audit service. Preapproval covers only services the Act allows.
Corporate responsibility: merging Sections 302 and 906. Section 302 is the civil certification of each periodic report; Section 906 is the criminal one, with knowing and willful penalty tiers.
Corporate responsibility: putting a Section 404 report in a quarterly filing, or giving the assessment to the auditor. Management assesses internal control annually, as of fiscal year-end.
SEC and enforcement: expecting the SEC to bring criminal charges or settle them. Its tools are civil; criminal cases belong to the Justice Department.
SEC and enforcement: using the 2002 text of Section 806. Since Dodd-Frank, a retaliation complaint has 180 days, not 90.
Frameworks and scope: rating a control deficiency by the errors found. A material weakness turns on the reasonable possibility of a material misstatement going undetected.
Frameworks and scope: mixing up editions. COSO 2013 has 17 principles under five components; ERM 2017 has 20 principles; the 1992 internal control edition is history.

sources.label: 17 CFR 240.12b-2 (filer categories and material weakness), Cornell LII

sections.title: Practice questions and mocks
sections.summary: SOXCPA sends no sample questions, so all practice material, KaiSip's included, is unofficial. KaiSip's timed mock is practice in the real format, and its score is not SOXCPA's.
items: SOXCPA does not send sample questions or past exams, and your own exam is not available for review afterward.
KaiSip's questions are original, written from the public law in the published format: four responses, one best answer and both question forms.
KaiSip's timed CSOE mock is practice: 35 questions in 90 minutes, answered in order and forward only, with no going back, as on the real exam.
A KaiSip mock score is not a SOXCPA score and cannot predict your result. On a short exam, one score can swing from one sitting to the next.
The exam asks only what SOXCPA's presentations clearly answer, and KaiSip has not seen them. Use KaiSip alongside the presentations, not instead of them.
After each practice set, read every explanation and note which rule each miss turned on: the actor, the section, the date, the number or the scope.

sections.title: Buying the program and fees
sections.summary: You buy the CSOE program from SOXCPA for one all-inclusive price. It covers the official presentations, your exam attempts and the certificate.
items: Price: US$147, a one-time, all-inclusive fee. SOXCPA says there is no additional cost for this program, now or later.
You can ask for a full refund within 60 days of payment.
No prerequisites, and SOXCPA membership is not required.
Up to three exam attempts a year are included at no extra cost.
There is no fixed exam date. SOXCPA's pages differ on how long you have: the FAQ PDF gives 4 years from payment, while the program page says your account does not expire. Plan on the shorter period.
The terms in force when you buy apply for 18 months from payment. If you sit the exam after that, the terms in force on that day apply.
steps: Read the program page and its terms, then buy the CSOE program from SOXCPA.
Watch your email: SOXCPA sends the presentations within 24 hours of payment, and the message may land in a spam or junk folder.
Study the presentations. SOXCPA advises going through them at least twice and estimates about 29 hours on average.
When you are ready, request your exam access as described in the next section.

sources.label: SOXCPA: Questions about the certification and the exams (PDF)

sections.title: Online only, from home or office
sections.summary: There are no test centers. You sit the CSOE online, from home or office in any country, on an online testing application, using exam credentials that SOXCPA emails to you.
items: You choose when to sit the exam. When you are ready, you email SOXCPA, at the address in its exam steps PDF, to ask for your exam username and password.
In that email, give your full name exactly as it should appear on your certificate, and your email address.
SOXCPA replies within 1 to 2 business days with a username, a password and account details for the testing application.
Before you start, read the terms on screen: the time limit, the back button, restarting and skipping.
KaiSip's advice: use a reliable internet connection and a device that will not update or restart during the exam, since closing the browser ends the attempt.
steps: Email SOXCPA to request your exam username and password, with your full name for the certificate and your email address.
Wait 1 to 2 business days for your username, password and account details.
Sign in to the online testing application with those details.
Choose to take a test, open the list of tests, and start the CSOE exam once you have read its terms.

sources.label: SOXCPA: Questions about the certification and the exams (PDF)

sections.title: Exam day
sections.summary: Pick a quiet time with 90 free minutes and a stable connection. Once you start, the clock runs and the exam moves forward only.
items: Have your materials ready before you start: PDFs open and bookmarked, and your one-page list of numbers to hand.
Answer every question in the order shown. You cannot skip, go back or pause.
Do not use the browser's back button, and do not close the browser. Closing it loses your answers and counts as an unsuccessful attempt.
Finish within 90 minutes, or the result is marked as an unsuccessful attempt.
On each question, look for the best answer: cross out the responses you know are wrong, then choose among the rest.

sections.title: After the exam
sections.summary: Your result, pass or fail, appears on screen when you finish. The exam and its questions are not available for review afterward.
items: The screen shows whether you passed or failed as soon as you finish.
If you pass, SOXCPA emails you within 1 to 2 business days with the next steps.
If you do not pass, you can take a second attempt, and then a third, with the same username, password and account details.
After a third unsuccessful attempt, there is a waiting period. A year after your first exam, you can email SOXCPA again and get three more attempts at no extra cost.
For security reasons, neither the exam nor its individual questions are available for review after the exam.
Before another attempt, go back to the rules your practice misses turned on, and study those parts of the presentations again.

sections.title: Becoming certified
sections.summary: Passing the exam makes you a Certified Sarbanes-Oxley Expert (CSOE). The certificate follows by email, and it does not expire.
items: Your certificate arrives by email as a PDF 7 business days after you pass. SOXCPA does not send printed certificates.
The certificate carries a QR code. Scanning it opens a SOXCPA web page for you that lists your name and certificates, so employers and others can check it is genuine.
The certificate has lifetime validity: no renewal fees, no recertification and no need to retake the exam.
SOXCPA invites certified members to keep up with changes through its reading room and newsletter at no cost. Laws and rules keep changing, so keep current.
The name on your certificate is the one you give when you request exam access, so check it carefully then.
